neighbours.label: word stem split before an '-es' suffix (Launch|es, crush|es, toothbrush|es)
fire: Every spring the agency launches a new campaign for road safety.
Most toothbrushes are made of plastic and nylon bristles.
The machine crushes the stones into fine gravel within minutes.
Several tornadoes touched down across the plains on Tuesday night.
The startup launches its first product in three European markets.
Heavy snow crushes the roofs of old barns almost every winter.
Dentists recommend replacing toothbrushes every three months.
Local reporters followed the tornadoes as they moved east.
quiet: Last spring the agency launched a new campaign for road safety.
Most combs are made of plastic and sometimes of polished wood.
The machine crushed the stones into fine gravel within minutes.
Several storms touched down across the plains on Tuesday night.
The startup will launch its first product in three European markets.
Heavy snow damaged the roofs of old barns almost every winter.
Dentists recommend replacing your brush every three months.
Local reporters followed the storm as it moved east.

notes: Output direction of this pole promotes 'es'/'ات'; fires on the stem token that awaits a plural/verb suffix.
